question.text: Ms. Kavitha Raman's Cat I AIF-VCF invests in pre-Series-A SaaS startups. Her portfolio company Aether Tech is 4 years old with INR 30 crore in turnover, working on an AI-driven supply-chain product. Per the DPIIT definition of 'startup' referenced in NISM Ch 2.3.1, does Aether Tech still qualify as a startup?

answer.text: No — DPIIT classifies a company as startup only if it is less than 3 years old.
Yes — DPIIT defines a startup as a company not more than 10 years old with turnover not exceeding INR 100 crore in any financial year, and engaged in innovation/scalability.
No — turnover above INR 25 crore disqualifies a company from being a startup per DPIIT.
Yes, but only if it is registered as a Private Limited Company under the Companies Act 2013 and generates no revenue.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Chapter 2.3.1, DPIIT defines a startup as 'a business that is not more than 10 years old and has not recorded a turnover of more than INR 100 crore in any financial year' and that is engaged in innovation/development/improvement of products or a scalable business model. Aether Tech at 4 years and INR 30 crore comfortably meets both limbs. **The Trap:** Option A uses the older 5-year DPIIT definition that was superseded. Option B mis-states the turnover ceiling (it is INR 100 crore, not INR 25 crore). Option D adds a zero-revenue requirement that does not exist — DPIIT allows turnover up to 100 crore. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) tests this for client suitability. Nothing similar in XIX-B or XXI-B. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When sourcing pre-Series-A deals, always verify DPIIT registration in the data room. Lost DPIIT status mid-investment horizon kills the Sec 80-IAC tax benefit for the investee and can complicate your AIF's claim to being a 'VCF' under AIF Regulation 2(1)(z).
